findings.passage: “It is my belief that election integrity is essential,” Bell said. “Upon someone’s death, the county registrar will be notified to remove that individual from the roll. That process being done quickly will prevent someone from taking on that individual’s identity possibly to commit voter fraud.”
findings.note: Quoted by a Tyler TV station when he announced HB 1264 for the filing session. He ties faster removal of deceased voters from the rolls to preventing identity theft and voter fraud.

findings.motion: HB 1264, time for reporting deceased residents to the voter registrar and the secretary of state (filed 2021-01-21; signed by the Governor 2021-06-04)
findings.note: He is the author. The bill sets the time for reporting deceased residents to the voter registrar and the secretary of state. The bill history shows it passed both chambers and was signed on 2021-06-04, effective 2021-09-01.

findings.motion: SB 7 (87th regular session), election integrity and security: listed as House cosponsor

findings.motion: SB 7 (87th regular session): passed by the House, Record 848, 78 yeas, 64 nays
findings.note: The House Journal lists K. Bell among the yeas on passage of SB 7, relating to elections, including election integrity and security.

findings.motion: SB 1 (87th 2nd called session): passed by the House, Record 61, 80 yeas, 41 nays
findings.note: The House Journal lists K. Bell among the yeas on passage of SB 1, the election integrity and security bill. This is the passage vote, separate from the conference-report vote already on file.

findings.motion: HB 5337, proof of citizenship to register to vote: coauthor (committee report sent to Calendars 2025-05-07)
findings.note: He is listed as a House coauthor of HB 5337, relating to requiring a person to submit proof of citizenship to register to vote and creating criminal offenses. The bill history shows the committee report sent to the calendar on 2025-05-07.

findings.motion: SJR 37, constitutional amendment clarifying that a voter must be a United States citizen: adopted by the House, Record 2196, 102 yeas, 14 nays, 22 present not voting
findings.note: The House Journal lists K. Bell among the yeas on final House adoption of SJR 37, the proposed amendment clarifying that a voter must be a United States citizen.
